limitations: Not a comprehensive opposition-research dossier, donor ledger, or full legislative voting inventory.
No unsubstantiated hidden scandal is alleged.
Historical donors, business investors, paid clients, organizations, and prospective political supporters are distinguished.

A report or committee finding is not automatically a criminal adjudication.

forecast_methodology.type: Subjective predictive scenario wargame with structured opposition
forecast_methodology.target: Conditional probability of winning the 2028 Republican nomination given that one of the eight authorized candidates wins; not full-field odds.
forecast_methodology.precision_note: Two-decimal arithmetic reproduces the mixture and preserves the total; it does not establish predictive precision.
forecast_methodology.normalization: The eight authorized candidates sum to 100. Prior five-candidate snapshots remain historical and are not directly comparable. Further roster changes require explicit authorization.
forecast_methodology.base_case: Persistent policy costs and accountability pressure; alternative recovery, selective blame and partisan-backlash branches are explicitly weighted.
forecast_methodology.probability_source: Weighted mixture of explicit scenario weights and conditional winner shares, incorporating candidate entry and organization. Inputs are analyst judgments, not calibrated frequencies.

candidate_inclusion_rule.assessment_note: Supersedes the imported >10% automatic inclusion rule. Outside contenders may be flagged for owner review, never added or assigned tracked probabilities by scheduled reviews.

authorization.basis: Predictive reasoning about voter attribution, candidate reactions and oversight is authorized under this dated methodology revision; roster changes require separate authorization.

forecast_methodology.formula: share(candidate) = sum over scenarios of weight_pct * shares_pct[candidate] / 100; both layers are conditional on an approved candidate winning.

wargame.target: Conditional probability of winning the 2028 Republican nomination given that one of the five included candidates wins; not a full-field probability.
wargame.horizon: Dominant environment during candidate entry, coalition formation and the 2028 Republican nomination contest; next checkpoints through early 2027.
wargame.summary: Vance retains the strongest starting route but loses some advantage once persistent costs, senior responsibility and a credible alternative are explicitly weighed. DeSantis becomes the leading approved alternative. Neither a disloyalty trap nor a successful Trump-authorized reset is inevitable.
wargame.debate_mode: Single-analyst review of competing cases, with an explicit rebuttal and verdict.
wargame.partition_rule: Branches describe the dominant nomination environment, conditional on an approved candidate winning. If drivers overlap, classify by what dominates coalition formation: substantive recovery first; otherwise broad senior accountability, accepted selective accountability, weak-findings partisan backlash, or the residual mixed-cost environment. Do not count the same world twice.
wargame.field_risk: A leadership crisis could favor an unlisted contender rather than any approved alternative. These conditional weights cannot measure that missing probability; no contender is added or assigned full-field odds.
wargame.weighting_note: Scenario weights and within-scenario winner shares are explicit subjective judgments, including entry/organization risk. Their weighted mixture is reproducible but uncalibrated. None is a poll conversion, measured decline, criminal-guilt estimate or confidence interval. No imported percentage is an anchor that must be preserved.

election_verdict.finding: The leading explanation is rejection of costly policy outcomes and self-serving priorities, amplified by weak candidates; this is not merely an unlucky campaign or a mandate against every conservative policy.
election_verdict.countercase: A midterm electorate differs from the next presidential primary electorate. Opposition turnout and local candidate quality can magnify a national defeat.
election_verdict.resolution: Treat affordability, war costs and accountability as a joint liability. Vance’s war-only diagnosis preserves his domestic program but leaves an opening on tariffs and administration priorities. Do not assign causal percentages from a survey.

responsibility.finding: Trump is the principal owner. Vance and Rubio cannot shed public advocacy and senior-office responsibility through retrospective criticism; Hegseth is a plausible concentrated target but not a sufficient explanation for economy-wide discontent.
responsibility.countercase: Voters can distinguish the president who ordered a policy, its operational managers and an adviser who argued for limits. A successful exit can differentiate the latter.
responsibility.resolution: Assign blame by the specific act, public defense and documentary chain, not association alone. Expect attempted scapegoating; whether it sticks depends on records and whether living conditions improve.

appeal_and_durability.finding: Vance has the strongest demonstrated starting route among the approved five. DeSantis has the clearest conditional opening for executive experience outside the current federal decision chain, but no demonstrated transfer of that coalition.
appeal_and_durability.countercase: Early recognition and patron access can be mistaken for durable attraction. An apparent outsider can also carry Trump-era baggage, past campaign weaknesses or state controversies.
appeal_and_durability.resolution: Discount familiar names and access when estimating future wins. A credible break needs a program, organizing and costly choices, while a continuity candidate needs results rather than a revised explanation.

democratic_power.finding: Expect investigations, preservation disputes, hearings and pressure over spending and confirmations once the new Congress organizes. This should keep responsibility and financial conflicts in the news rather than permit a clean messaging reset.
democratic_power.countercase: A congressional majority is not control of the executive. Vetoes, Senate procedure, litigation, competing legislative priorities and public fatigue constrain what Democrats can deliver.
democratic_power.resolution: Forecast sustained scrutiny more readily than immediate policy reversal, removal or prosecution. Obstruction or partisan excess can create a Republican rallying point; failure to lower costs can also redistribute blame toward Congress.

oversight_findings.finding: Politically damaging records about process, internal warnings and financial conflicts are more plausible than a uniform exoneration. A proven criminal case against any named contender is not established and is not the base-case requirement for political harm.
oversight_findings.countercase: An inquiry can repeat already-known allegations, encounter privilege or missing records, or fail to connect a conflict to a decision. Strong partisan rhetoric can outrun admissible evidence.
oversight_findings.resolution: Model systemic damage, selective accountability and weak-findings backlash separately. Criminal illegality, a substantiated ethics violation, misleading conduct and political embarrassment are different outcomes; do not forecast a particular person’s guilt from incentives.

loyalty_dilemma.finding: Selective differentiation is the most likely initial strategy: credit Trump and MAGA goals, blame implementation or advisers, promise competent correction. Vance’s timing makes an opportunism attack available to both hawks and restraint rivals.
loyalty_dilemma.countercase: Trump publicly welcomed Vance’s postmortem and Don Jr. supported the message in the existing record. Vance can criticize policy with permission; voters need not punish adaptation they see as learning.
loyalty_dilemma.resolution: The squeeze is real but not automatically fatal. The critical test is a costly forced choice: testimony, a funding limit, a dismissal or contradiction in documents. A debate attack matters if a credible rival and an audience amplify it, not merely because the line is available.

scenarios.name: Results rehabilitate continuity
scenarios.definition: A durable improvement in war and household costs dominates the nomination environment; serious revelations do not prevent leadership rehabilitation.
scenarios.weight_reason: Lower weight than persistent costs because an exit alone does not reverse inflation or repair trust; retained because two years allow meaningful change.
scenarios.sequence: Negotiation or policy correction produces visible relief; Trump claims vindication; networks consolidate behind an heir.
scenarios.falsifier: A settlement without cost relief or continuing credible records of misconduct would defeat the rehabilitation premise.

candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A demand for a wholly new figure remains small.

scenarios.name: Costs persist; leadership retains a coalition
scenarios.definition: Neither recovery, systemic accountability, a convincing selective reset nor an oversight backlash becomes dominant; dissatisfaction persists but Republican leadership retains organizing capacity.
scenarios.weight_reason: A residual mixed environment is plausible: entrenched networks survive, while prolonged costs prevent a clean return to the inherited baseline.
scenarios.sequence: Voters remain dissatisfied; candidates selectively criticize execution; no rival fully coordinates defectors.
scenarios.falsifier: Clear rehabilitation, party-wide documentary repudiation or a successful scapegoat reset would move weight to another branch.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: He can adapt, but recurring costs and credibility attacks reduce his cushion.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: A loyalist alternative persists, limited by policy responsibility and entry.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: Distance offers a meaningful but unproven coordination point.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: Tariff skepticism helps at the margin; hawkish overlap limits growth.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A niche exists but organizing is missing.

scenarios.name: Accountability discredits the federal leadership
scenarios.definition: Credible disclosures or durable policy failure attach responsibility to senior leadership; a subordinate-only explanation does not satisfy an important Republican constituency. Criminal convictions are not required.
scenarios.weight_reason: War, household costs, demand for checks and documented investigative preparation justify substantial weight; absence of post-election primary data prevents making this the sole or majority scenario.
scenarios.sequence: Records or continued failure expose contradictions; donors and organizers consider alternatives; a credible rival turns attacks into coordination and early-state gains.
scenarios.falsifier: If primary voters retain confidence, disclosures fail to connect to senior decisions, or no alternative organizes, this branch is overstated.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: He retains a floor of access, but joint ownership and contradictory defenses are costly.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: Direct foreign-policy ownership and deference leave limited escape.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: An experienced state executive is the strongest approved coordination point, conditional on rebuilding.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: He offers a non-executive fallback, discounted for hawkish responsibility.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A leadership vacuum helps a niche challenger, heavily discounted for insider baggage and entry gates.

scenarios.name: Blame concentrates; an heir survives a reset
scenarios.definition: Credible accountability is concentrated on specific officials and accepted as bounded; correction creates space for a successor without broad leadership rehabilitation.
scenarios.weight_reason: Personnel pressure makes scapegoating plausible, but replacing a minister cannot alone erase prices, tariffs or vice-presidential responsibility.
scenarios.sequence: Hearings or a dismissal concentrate blame; Trump authorizes correction; an heir claims limits and competence while rivals test whether separation is credible.
scenarios.falsifier: Documents implicating the heir, continued economic deterioration or failed separation would push toward systemic damage or managed costs.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: Vance can support accountability with Trump’s permission; he is not inherently trapped on every choice.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: Hegseth-focused blame does not automatically absolve State advice or Rubio’s defenses.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: A partial reset leaves room to argue Washington cannot police itself.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: A fallback benefits if rival heirs remain compromised.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A small opening persists without demonstrated electoral scale.

scenarios.name: Weak findings and partisan conflict restore loyalty
scenarios.definition: Investigations fail to persuade enough Republican voters and conflict with Democrats becomes the dominant organizing frame, without a substantive recovery.
scenarios.weight_reason: Retained as a countercase, not equal-weight balance: the documented demand for oversight makes assuming immediate backlash too optimistic for incumbents.
scenarios.sequence: Evidence disappoints or Democrats overreach; Republicans rally against Congress; Trump’s endorsement regains coordinating force.
scenarios.falsifier: Credible corroborated findings accepted within Republican networks or effective Democratic delivery would weaken this branch.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: The best-positioned authorized heir benefits, conditional on Trump maintaining permission.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: A loyalist campaign has room, though deference remains an entry constraint.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: A rupture pitch loses demand; he must compete on conservative governing performance.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: An ideological lane survives but coordination favors the heir.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A media-oriented alternative may gain attention but not necessarily delegates.

jd_vance.best_case: He retains fundraising, name recognition and succession channels while delivering a negotiated exit. Trump grants room to correct the policy; primary voters prefer an experienced heir to restarting the party.
jd_vance.failure_case: Post-defeat criticism looks retrospective. Documents or a Hegseth confrontation force him to defend conduct he privately questioned, abandon a colleague, or evade. Rivals use that record to make both loyalty and restraint claims untrustworthy.
jd_vance.rebuttal: The opposing case overstates a no-win trap. Trump can authorize blame of subordinates; replacing Hegseth could help Vance. Without compelling records or a viable rival, voters may reward a practical pivot rather than consistency.
jd_vance.verdict: Keep him first, but reduce the inherited near-half share. Organizational advantages survive many branches; a material chance of sustained responsibility and credible opposition narrows his lead. The downgrade is a new judgment, not a measured fall in primary support.
jd_vance.entry_assessment: A presidential run is plausible from the vice presidency, but not declared here. Trump’s endorsement, rehabilitation and whether the lane remains viable determine entry and success; these are incorporated in scenario shares.
jd_vance.next_move: Likely defend Trump personally while emphasizing an exit, costs and his earlier doubts. On Hegseth, initially separate policy review and due process from personal loyalty; reassess if evidence implicates his own public account.
jd_vance.rival_attack: A rival can contrast private objections, public defenses and the timing after defeat: why trust another pivot? A hawk can attack abandonment; a restrainer can demand proof of a costly pre-election objection.
jd_vance.durability_test: Actual peace and lower costs would blunt a consistency attack. Repeated incompatible defenses, documentary contradiction or loss of Trump-backed organizers would make the squeeze consequential rather than rhetorical.

marco_rubio.best_case: An experienced security official can inherit loyalists who distrust Vance’s pivot, draw on hawkish donor access and argue the problem was execution rather than the original objectives.
marco_rubio.failure_case: If the policy itself is repudiated, credentials become ownership. Hearings put his explanations alongside internal warnings, while deference to Vance or failure to enter prevents conversion of donor preference into a campaign.
marco_rubio.rebuttal: Republicans can retain support for the original intervention despite rejecting its costs. Vance may absorb more succession blame, and Rubio can benefit if a settlement vindicates the security rationale.
marco_rubio.verdict: Lower than the imported share: his strongest assets overlap the policy most directly under challenge, and entry/deference uncertainty remains. He still has a real recovery or loyalty-based route.
marco_rubio.entry_assessment: Current office and donor preferences do not establish an independent candidacy. Explicit prior deference to Vance makes a contested entry less assured.
marco_rubio.next_move: Likely defend the initial security rationale, emphasize an achievable end state and avoid an early campaign declaration. Whether he protects or distances from Hegseth depends on evidence and departmental responsibility.
marco_rubio.rival_attack: An outsider can ask why the foreign-policy expert did not anticipate the costs. Vance can claim to have offered the exit while Rubio defended the initial course.
marco_rubio.durability_test: Watch an independent fundraising/endorsement operation, entry statements and testimony tying advice to decisions. A defensible settlement strengthens his case; proof public claims diverged from internal assessments weakens it.

ron_desantis.best_case: He offers governing experience without current federal command responsibility. Donors and primary voters seeking a new direction can coordinate around him if Washington’s leaders remain discredited.
ron_desantis.failure_case: Distance is mistaken for popularity. His earlier intervention statements, state accountability exposure and past campaign problems prevent a clean break, while donors prefer someone outside the approved roster.
ron_desantis.rebuttal: Those weaknesses do not erase the contrast with incumbents who must defend federal decisions. A prolonged accountability cycle can change what primary voters value and make executive distance more useful than Washington access.
ron_desantis.verdict: Raise him to the leading approved alternative, not an established new favorite. The gain is concentrated in systemic-repudiation branches and remains dependent on rebuilding an actual campaign.
ron_desantis.entry_assessment: A renewed run and effective organization are possible, not assumed certain. Shares discount the risk of non-entry, failed rebuilding and selection of another alternative.
ron_desantis.next_move: Likely distinguish limited force from prolonged war, emphasize state governing competence and criticize Washington without making an immediate personal break with Trump.
ron_desantis.rival_attack: Vance can cite prior support for force and the failed earlier campaign. Rivals can test whether state controversies undermine an accountability pitch.
ron_desantis.durability_test: Require current donors, organizers, early-state activity and voter response to the contrast; absence of those developments should erode the inferred opening.

ted_cruz.best_case: He has a recognizable conservative identity and a tariff-skeptical argument on costs. As a non-executive contender he can exploit division between administration heirs and seek religious-conservative organization.
ted_cruz.failure_case: A hawkish record limits separation from intervention, Rubio competes for donors and recognition does not produce coalition growth. Past repositioning and judgment controversies remain usable.
ted_cruz.rebuttal: Rubio may defer or remain tied to official explanations, leaving Cruz an independent lane. Opposition to tariffs can fit the election’s economic lesson without rejecting conservative identity.
ted_cruz.verdict: A modest relative gain as a fallback when executive contenders lose credibility, capped by shared policy exposure and unverified current organizing. No automatic transfer of Rubio donors is assumed.
ted_cruz.entry_assessment: A third presidential effort is uncertain; no new campaign or current donor coalition is verified in this pass.
ted_cruz.next_move: Likely criticize economic execution and tariff costs while defending security commitments and preserving access to Trump-aligned voters.
ted_cruz.rival_attack: Rivals can ask how a hawkish alternative escapes the same war verdict, and why this campaign would consolidate support his previous effort did not.
ted_cruz.durability_test: A distinct cost-of-living coalition and current organizational commitments matter more than recycled 2016 donor names.

john_mcentee.best_case: Personnel and withdrawal experience can support a substantive nationalist challenge when established contenders fail; a smaller media-driven opening can become electorally useful if organization follows.
john_mcentee.failure_case: He is himself a Trump-era insider. Prior conduct, electoral-count work and business scrutiny complicate a clean-accountability pitch, and historical business financing does not supply a campaign.
john_mcentee.rebuttal: Lack of an established campaign is not proof of absent political substance. A discredited leadership can make operational knowledge and a coherent restraint case attractive to a niche that later grows.
john_mcentee.verdict: Keep a small speculative share, with only a modest gain in a more open race. Do not reward him mechanically for every Vance weakness; the opening may go outside this roster.
john_mcentee.entry_assessment: Entry, financing and a delegate operation are all unestablished. These gates substantially suppress the share in every branch.
john_mcentee.next_move: If seeking the opening, likely emphasize personnel control and withdrawal work while trying to distinguish substantive loyalty to a program from defense of every Trump decision.
john_mcentee.rival_attack: Rivals can point to his own insider history, January 6 record and commercial ties, and ask for proof he can build a national electoral organization.
john_mcentee.durability_test: Require direct current positions, entry signals, independent political funding and organizers. Media audience or a shared Thiel connection alone is insufficient.

predictions.claim: Vance will initially combine personal loyalty to Trump with policy differentiation rather than make an explicit personal rupture.
predictions.likelihood: More likely than a personal break; analyst judgment.
predictions.test: Review direct statements through February 1 for both continued personal support and criticism/correction of war policy. An explicit repudiation of Trump’s leadership contradicts the predicted initial strategy; no accessible statements leaves it unresolved.
predictions.resolution: Future test; no post-election primary-support change is assumed.

predictions.claim: The new Congress will sustain an accountability agenda, but findings and removal will lag preservation demands.
predictions.likelihood: Investigative escalation is likely; a specific removal or criminal finding is not predicted.
predictions.test: Check committee organization and at least one hearing, subpoena or document production in the named inquiries. Record obstruction, new proof and any official adjudication separately. No escalation by April 1 contradicts the agenda forecast.
predictions.resolution: Official notices establish preparation, not the future outcome.

predictions.claim: DeSantis will not yet have overtaken Vance in comparable national Republican nomination polls by early April 2027.
predictions.likelihood: A material risk of failed coordination remains even if dissatisfaction persists.
predictions.test: Among at least three post-election national Republican nomination polls fielded by April 1 that list both, check whether DeSantis leads Vance in a majority. A majority lead contradicts this expectation; fewer than three qualifying polls leaves it unresolved. Track current donor commitments and early-state organization separately to explain the result.
predictions.resolution: Future test of whether an inferred alternative opening has become measured preference; no current transfer has been verified.

gaps: Scenario weights and conditional shares are subjective and uncalibrated; arithmetic does not validate the inputs.
No post-election primary candidate poll, full FEC audit, new entry commitment or early-state organizational audit was verified. Existing historical evidence remains dated.
Freshly read AP election survey and official preservation demands inform the environment. Candidate policy and conduct records are carried from the prior pass, not wholly reverified.
Search results suggested newer Vance diplomacy and Democratic priorities stories, but full pages failed to load; they were not used as verified updates.
The election survey describes the midterm electorate, not the next primary electorate or a causal decomposition of vote choice.
Unlisted-field risk is material and unquantified; no nominees were added.

history.summary: Vance retains the strongest starting route in the expanded field. DeSantis and Kemp compete for a conservative executive reset; Paul and Massie contest overlapping restraint and constitutional-limit audiences. Entry, party route and organization remain material gates. This establishes a new eight-person baseline; percentage-point changes from the five-person field are not comparable.

jd_vance.reason: The strongest established succession route still leads, but the expanded field offers more credible executive and policy alternatives. Success depends on results, credible differentiation and coalition retention; this is a new eight-person baseline, not a measured fall in support.

faction_links.mechanism: The existing finance role, fundraiser and organization build a candidate channel; his public war postmortem gives the lane a distinct succession argument without proving voter conversion.
Historical patronage supplies access, but continued support and policy agreement must be assessed separately.

marco_rubio.reason: A credible security and loyalist alternative, limited by ownership of war policy, entry/deference uncertainty and competing non-executive challengers. Donor access does not establish current campaign commitments.

faction_links.mechanism: State/NSC access and donor preference preserve a rival route; public war defense gives hawks an alternative to Vance but limits separation from administration costs.

ron_desantis.reason: The largest approved executive-reset alternative, but Kemp now competes for that same demand. National campaign rebuilding, accountability exposure and actual coalition coordination determine whether the opening is realized.

ted_cruz.reason: A smaller conservative fallback with tariff skepticism and hawkish networks. Rubio competes for those networks, while Paul and Massie offer different policy critiques; no automatic transfer of donor or voter support is assumed.

faction_links.mechanism: Donor-facing positioning distinguishes him from Vance; the same hawkish networks also court Rubio, so factional preference is not an exclusive candidate coalition.

john_mcentee.reason: A small speculative path based on personnel and withdrawal experience, constrained by entry, organization and insider baggage. Additional experienced alternatives weaken any assumption that leadership failure flows to him.

faction_links.mechanism: Historical personnel recruitment offers an executive-control capability relevant to this faction’s goals; that is a policy-channel analogy, not evidence that its current leaders support his nomination.
His actual 2020 withdrawal directive work could contest an exclusive claim to demonstrated restraint; no current endorsement, alliance or bloc of primary votes follows.

rand_paul.reason: A meaningful alternative, below the leading executive contenders because coalition breadth and entry remain uncertain. Do not treat all business or anti-war voters as his supporters.

faction_links.mechanism: Existing policy dissent and oversight channels support an analytical campaign argument; inclusion in the forecast does not establish an endorsement, new faction alignment or voter transfer.

brian_kemp.reason: A substantial alternative, competing especially with DeSantis for the executive-reset lane. Entry uncertainty and an unverified national organization prevent treating home-state enthusiasm as a national mandate.

thomas_massie.reason: A small, substantive challenger with substantial entry and party-route risk. The forecast does not count an independent run as a Republican nomination win or duplicate Paul’s potential coalition.

faction_links.mechanism: Existing policy dissent and oversight channels support an analytical campaign argument; inclusion in the forecast does not establish an endorsement, new faction alignment or voter transfer.

wargame.target: Conditional probability of winning the 2028 Republican nomination given that one of the eight authorized candidates wins; not full-field odds.
wargame.horizon: Dominant environment during candidate entry, coalition formation and the 2028 Republican nomination contest; next checkpoints through early 2027.
wargame.summary: Vance retains the strongest starting route in the expanded field. DeSantis and Kemp compete for a conservative executive reset; Paul and Massie contest overlapping restraint and constitutional-limit audiences. Entry, party route and organization remain material gates.
wargame.debate_mode: Single-analyst review of competing cases, with an explicit rebuttal and verdict.
wargame.partition_rule: Branches describe the dominant nomination environment, conditional on an approved candidate winning. If drivers overlap, classify by what dominates coalition formation: substantive recovery first; otherwise broad senior accountability, accepted selective accountability, weak-findings partisan backlash, or the residual mixed-cost environment. Do not count the same world twice.
wargame.field_risk: Eight authorized contenders are modeled. Unlisted contenders can still win; influence or an independent presidential run does not count as winning the Republican nomination. No full-field residual is estimated.
wargame.weighting_note: Scenario weights and within-scenario winner shares are explicit subjective judgments, including entry/organization risk. Their weighted mixture is reproducible but uncalibrated. None is a poll conversion, measured decline, criminal-guilt estimate or confidence interval. No imported percentage is an anchor that must be preserved. This is an owner-authorized roster rebase: old five-person percentages and new eight-person percentages have different denominators. The same scenario environments/weights are retained, with within-scenario shares reassessed for the added competition; it is not a measured change in voter support.

election_verdict.finding: The leading explanation is rejection of costly policy outcomes and self-serving priorities, amplified by weak candidates; this is not merely an unlucky campaign or a mandate against every conservative policy.
election_verdict.countercase: A midterm electorate differs from the next presidential primary electorate. Opposition turnout and local candidate quality can magnify a national defeat.
election_verdict.resolution: Treat affordability, war costs and accountability as a joint liability. Vance’s war-only diagnosis preserves his domestic program but leaves an opening on tariffs and administration priorities. Do not assign causal percentages from a survey.

responsibility.finding: Trump is the principal owner. Vance and Rubio cannot shed public advocacy and senior-office responsibility through retrospective criticism; Hegseth is a plausible concentrated target but not a sufficient explanation for economy-wide discontent.
responsibility.countercase: Voters can distinguish the president who ordered a policy, its operational managers and an adviser who argued for limits. A successful exit can differentiate the latter.
responsibility.resolution: Assign blame by the specific act, public defense and documentary chain, not association alone. Expect attempted scapegoating; whether it sticks depends on records and whether living conditions improve.

appeal_and_durability.finding: Vance has the strongest demonstrated starting route among the eight approved contenders. DeSantis and Kemp compete for executive competence outside the federal decision chain; Paul and Massie offer distinct but overlapping constitutional-limit challenges. No coalition transfer is yet demonstrated.
appeal_and_durability.countercase: Early recognition and patron access can be mistaken for durable attraction. An apparent outsider can also carry Trump-era baggage, past campaign weaknesses or state controversies.
appeal_and_durability.resolution: Discount familiar names and access when estimating future wins. A credible break needs a program, organizing and costly choices, while a continuity candidate needs results rather than a revised explanation.

democratic_power.finding: Expect investigations, preservation disputes, hearings and pressure over spending and confirmations once the new Congress organizes. This should keep responsibility and financial conflicts in the news rather than permit a clean messaging reset.
democratic_power.countercase: A congressional majority is not control of the executive. Vetoes, Senate procedure, litigation, competing legislative priorities and public fatigue constrain what Democrats can deliver.
democratic_power.resolution: Forecast sustained scrutiny more readily than immediate policy reversal, removal or prosecution. Obstruction or partisan excess can create a Republican rallying point; failure to lower costs can also redistribute blame toward Congress.

oversight_findings.finding: Politically damaging records about process, internal warnings and financial conflicts are more plausible than a uniform exoneration. A proven criminal case against any named contender is not established and is not the base-case requirement for political harm.
oversight_findings.countercase: An inquiry can repeat already-known allegations, encounter privilege or missing records, or fail to connect a conflict to a decision. Strong partisan rhetoric can outrun admissible evidence.
oversight_findings.resolution: Model systemic damage, selective accountability and weak-findings backlash separately. Criminal illegality, a substantiated ethics violation, misleading conduct and political embarrassment are different outcomes; do not forecast a particular person’s guilt from incentives.

loyalty_dilemma.finding: Selective differentiation is the most likely initial strategy: credit Trump and MAGA goals, blame implementation or advisers, promise competent correction. Vance’s timing makes an opportunism attack available to both hawks and restraint rivals.
loyalty_dilemma.countercase: Trump publicly welcomed Vance’s postmortem and Don Jr. supported the message in the existing record. Vance can criticize policy with permission; voters need not punish adaptation they see as learning.
loyalty_dilemma.resolution: The squeeze is real but not automatically fatal. The critical test is a costly forced choice: testimony, a funding limit, a dismissal or contradiction in documents. A debate attack matters if a credible rival and an audience amplify it, not merely because the line is available.

marco_rubio.failure_case: If the policy itself is repudiated, credentials become ownership. Hearings put his explanations alongside internal warnings, while deference to Vance or failure to enter prevents conversion of donor preference into a campaign.
marco_rubio.rebuttal: Republicans can retain support for the original intervention despite rejecting its costs. Vance may absorb more succession blame, and Rubio can benefit if a settlement vindicates the security rationale.
marco_rubio.verdict: A credible security and loyalist alternative, limited by ownership of war policy, entry/deference uncertainty and competing non-executive challengers. Donor access does not establish current campaign commitments.
marco_rubio.entry_assessment: Current office and donor preferences do not establish an independent candidacy. Explicit prior deference to Vance makes a contested entry less assured.
marco_rubio.next_move: Likely defend the initial security rationale, emphasize an achievable end state and avoid an early campaign declaration. Whether he protects or distances from Hegseth depends on evidence and departmental responsibility.
marco_rubio.rival_attack: An outsider can ask why the foreign-policy expert did not anticipate the costs. Vance can claim to have offered the exit while Rubio defended the initial course.
marco_rubio.durability_test: Watch an independent fundraising/endorsement operation, entry statements and testimony tying advice to decisions. A defensible settlement strengthens his case; proof public claims diverged from internal assessments weakens it.

ron_desantis.best_case: He offers governing experience without current federal command responsibility. Donors and primary voters seeking a new direction can coordinate around him if Washington’s leaders remain discredited.
ron_desantis.failure_case: Distance is mistaken for popularity. His earlier intervention statements, state accountability exposure and past campaign problems prevent a clean break, while donors prefer someone outside the approved roster.
ron_desantis.rebuttal: Those weaknesses do not erase the contrast with incumbents who must defend federal decisions. A prolonged accountability cycle can change what primary voters value and make executive distance more useful than Washington access.
ron_desantis.verdict: The largest approved executive-reset alternative, but Kemp now competes for that same demand. National campaign rebuilding, accountability exposure and actual coalition coordination determine whether the opening is realized.
ron_desantis.entry_assessment: A renewed run and effective organization are possible, not assumed certain. Shares discount the risk of non-entry, failed rebuilding and selection of another alternative.
ron_desantis.next_move: Likely distinguish limited force from prolonged war, emphasize state governing competence and criticize Washington without making an immediate personal break with Trump.
ron_desantis.rival_attack: Vance can cite prior support for force and the failed earlier campaign. Rivals can test whether state controversies undermine an accountability pitch.
ron_desantis.durability_test: Require current donors, organizers, early-state activity and voter response to the contrast; absence of those developments should erode the inferred opening.

ted_cruz.best_case: He has a recognizable conservative identity and a tariff-skeptical argument on costs. As a non-executive contender he can exploit division between administration heirs and seek religious-conservative organization.
ted_cruz.failure_case: A hawkish record limits separation from intervention, Rubio competes for donors and recognition does not produce coalition growth. Past repositioning and judgment controversies remain usable.
ted_cruz.rebuttal: Rubio may defer or remain tied to official explanations, leaving Cruz an independent lane. Opposition to tariffs can fit the election’s economic lesson without rejecting conservative identity.
ted_cruz.verdict: A smaller conservative fallback with tariff skepticism and hawkish networks. Rubio competes for those networks, while Paul and Massie offer different policy critiques; no automatic transfer of donor or voter support is assumed.
ted_cruz.entry_assessment: A third presidential effort is uncertain; no new campaign or current donor coalition is verified in this pass.
ted_cruz.next_move: Likely criticize economic execution and tariff costs while defending security commitments and preserving access to Trump-aligned voters.
ted_cruz.rival_attack: Rivals can ask how a hawkish alternative escapes the same war verdict, and why this campaign would consolidate support his previous effort did not.
ted_cruz.durability_test: A distinct cost-of-living coalition and current organizational commitments matter more than recycled 2016 donor names.

john_mcentee.best_case: Personnel and withdrawal experience can support a substantive nationalist challenge when established contenders fail; a smaller media-driven opening can become electorally useful if organization follows.
john_mcentee.failure_case: He is himself a Trump-era insider. Prior conduct, electoral-count work and business scrutiny complicate a clean-accountability pitch, and historical business financing does not supply a campaign.
john_mcentee.rebuttal: Lack of an established campaign is not proof of absent political substance. A discredited leadership can make operational knowledge and a coherent restraint case attractive to a niche that later grows.
john_mcentee.verdict: A small speculative path based on personnel and withdrawal experience, constrained by entry, organization and insider baggage. Additional experienced alternatives weaken any assumption that leadership failure flows to him.
john_mcentee.entry_assessment: Entry, financing and a delegate operation are all unestablished. These gates substantially suppress the share in every branch.
john_mcentee.next_move: If seeking the opening, likely emphasize personnel control and withdrawal work while trying to distinguish substantive loyalty to a program from defense of every Trump decision.
john_mcentee.rival_attack: Rivals can point to his own insider history, January 6 record and commercial ties, and ask for proof he can build a national electoral organization.
john_mcentee.durability_test: Require direct current positions, entry signals, independent political funding and organizers. Media audience or a shared Thiel connection alone is insufficient.

rand_paul.best_case: He unites constitutional restraint with free-trade business conservatives and points to dissent before the electoral defeat. A credible organization turns that argument into a broader corrective coalition.
rand_paul.failure_case: The audience remains narrow, overlaps Massie’s, or dislikes his small-government remedies. A proven critique does not produce enough organizers and delegates; he may not enter.
rand_paul.rebuttal: A leadership crisis can change which policies voters prioritize. His existing platform and political networks make him more than a hypothetical audience, even without evidence of a winning coalition.
rand_paul.verdict: A meaningful alternative, below the leading executive contenders because coalition breadth and entry remain uncertain. Do not treat all business or anti-war voters as his supporters.
rand_paul.entry_assessment: He has publicly considered a bid; inclusion is not a declaration. Entry and a national campaign remain gates to winning.
rand_paul.next_move: Likely emphasize costs, free trade and congressional limits while deciding whether a new coalition is available. Expect selective cooperation rather than assume every act is an absolute break with Trump.
rand_paul.rival_attack: Vance can demand a workable governing coalition and challenge whether fiscal restraint addresses household needs. Massie can contest which candidate best demonstrates costly dissent.
rand_paul.durability_test: Look for entry, named organizers, current funding and support beyond a liberty-oriented core. Review individual votes rather than accepting an image of perfect consistency.

brian_kemp.best_case: He offers conservative executive competence outside the federal decision chain. Business-oriented donors and voters seeking a reset coordinate around him rather than assume DeSantis owns that lane.
brian_kemp.failure_case: State approval does not transfer nationally, he declines to enter, or conservative policies and a national campaign expose weaknesses that the contrast with Washington concealed.
brian_kemp.rebuttal: A strong state constituency and governing record are concrete assets. If the administration’s heirs remain compromised, his distance can matter even without an established national campaign today.
brian_kemp.verdict: A substantial alternative, competing especially with DeSantis for the executive-reset lane. Entry uncertainty and an unverified national organization prevent treating home-state enthusiasm as a national mandate.
brian_kemp.entry_assessment: No presidential entry commitment is verified. The forecast discounts the possibility he declines again or fails to assemble a national operation.
brian_kemp.next_move: Likely test donor and early-state interest while emphasizing state outcomes and competent conservative government, avoiding immediate ownership of federal war arguments.
brian_kemp.rival_attack: DeSantis can claim the same governing lane; Trump-aligned rivals can question loyalty, while others scrutinize whether state policies match a broader renewal pitch.
brian_kemp.durability_test: National entry signals, current donor commitments and early-state support must validate the home-state foundation. Continued non-entry or failure of national transfer weakens the estimate.

thomas_massie.best_case: Subsequent evidence validates his war-powers and accountability arguments. His demonstrated dissent and some independent-support networks become a national insurgent platform.
thomas_massie.failure_case: His primary defeat reflects a limited Republican constituency, and the most plausible next move is another office or an outside-party project. Paul and larger campaigns absorb his potential support.
thomas_massie.rebuttal: Losing a Trump-targeted primary can demonstrate a costly break. His oversight actions give a challenge more substance than a media-only campaign, but that still must be converted into organization.
thomas_massie.verdict: A small, substantive challenger with substantial entry and party-route risk. The forecast does not count an independent run as a Republican nomination win or duplicate Paul’s potential coalition.
thomas_massie.entry_assessment: He left options open; a federal filing for a House race is not a presidential declaration. Both office and party route remain unresolved.
thomas_massie.next_move: Likely keep oversight and constitutional limits visible while preserving multiple political routes. Evidence produced by Democrats can strengthen his earlier argument without making him a Democratic ally.
thomas_massie.rival_attack: Rivals can point to his primary defeat and ask whether he has a national electorate or a protest audience. Paul can claim a broader platform for overlapping voters.
thomas_massie.durability_test: A clear GOP entry, organizers and a demonstrable constituency beyond his former district are essential. An outside-party route or another-office campaign should reduce his nomination share.

predictions.claim: Vance will initially combine personal loyalty to Trump with policy differentiation rather than make an explicit personal rupture.
predictions.likelihood: More likely than a personal break; analyst judgment.
predictions.test: Review direct statements through February 1 for both continued personal support and criticism/correction of war policy. An explicit repudiation of Trump’s leadership contradicts the predicted initial strategy; no accessible statements leaves it unresolved.
predictions.resolution: Future test; no post-election primary-support change is assumed.

predictions.claim: The new Congress will sustain an accountability agenda, but findings and removal will lag preservation demands.
predictions.likelihood: Investigative escalation is likely; a specific removal or criminal finding is not predicted.
predictions.test: Check committee organization and at least one hearing, subpoena or document production in the named inquiries. Record obstruction, new proof and any official adjudication separately. No escalation by April 1 contradicts the agenda forecast.
predictions.resolution: Official notices establish preparation, not the future outcome.

predictions.claim: DeSantis will not yet have overtaken Vance in comparable national Republican nomination polls by early April 2027.
predictions.likelihood: A material risk of failed coordination remains even if dissatisfaction persists.
predictions.test: Among at least three post-election national Republican nomination polls fielded by April 1 that list both, check whether DeSantis leads Vance in a majority. A majority lead contradicts this expectation; fewer than three qualifying polls leaves it unresolved. Track current donor commitments and early-state organization separately to explain the result.
predictions.resolution: Future test of whether an inferred alternative opening has become measured preference; no current transfer has been verified.

case_review.summary: Authorized roster expansion adds competitors within the existing environments, not a new news-driven weekly wargame. Retain the five scenarios and earlier prediction questions; revise within-scenario coalition competition.

recovery.reason: Retain the environment and weight; reassess winner shares for three newly authorized competing candidates.

managed_costs.reason: Retain the environment and weight; reassess winner shares for three newly authorized competing candidates.

systemic.reason: Retain the environment and weight; reassess winner shares for three newly authorized competing candidates.

selective.reason: Retain the environment and weight; reassess winner shares for three newly authorized competing candidates.

backlash.reason: Retain the environment and weight; reassess winner shares for three newly authorized competing candidates.

vance-selective-loyalty.reason: The original question remains observable; preserving it avoids moving historical goalposts.

congress-accountability.reason: The original question remains observable; preserving it avoids moving historical goalposts.

alternative-coordination.reason: The original question remains observable; preserving it avoids moving historical goalposts.

gaps: Targeted onboarding, not a full FEC, position or controversy audit. Specific profile gaps are labeled.
Carlson is excluded under the final authorization; his influence can still affect other contenders.
Kemp home-state approval is not national preference. Paul and Massie share potential audiences; neither inherits a whole faction automatically.
Paul’s PAC source full-page recheck returned 403. Massie’s entry transcript was read earlier but failed to reload; descriptions remain qualified.
Current donor commitments, national organization and actual entry remain unverified for the additions.
Historical five-person estimates are preserved; no cross-roster pp movement is claimed.

history.summary: Persistent costs and accountability pressure still compete with retained Republican organization. No automatic outsider transfer is established. Retain the five environments and provisional eight-person mixture after common comparison; exact ceilings and floors remain weakly identified.

jd_vance.reason: Provisional hold after common comparison. Trump-aligned voters overlap McEntee; policy-restraint voters overlap Paul and Massie. Recovery can coordinate these groups behind an heir, while persistent costs permit defections without automatically delivering them to one rival. 16–52 reflects a viable heir even under systemic damage and the strongest coordination route in recovery/backlash. The high floor is vulnerable to actual organizer defection or refusal to run; it is not a measured loyal bloc.

faction_links.mechanism: The existing finance role, fundraiser and organization build a candidate channel; his public war postmortem gives the lane a distinct succession argument without proving voter conversion.
Historical patronage supplies access, but continued support and policy agreement must be assessed separately.

marco_rubio.reason: Provisional hold after common comparison. Competes with Cruz for hawkish and business-oriented networks and with Vance for continuity. Those networks cannot be assigned fully to both Rubio and Cruz. 6–20 reflects weaker entry/permission and stronger federal policy ownership than governors, but a durable security constituency in recovery. Raise the ceiling if independent entry and committed organization appear.

faction_links.mechanism: State/NSC access and donor preference preserve a rival route; public war defense gives hawks an alternative to Vance but limits separation from administration costs.

ron_desantis.reason: Provisional hold after common comparison. Splits executive-reset demand with Kemp; both cannot receive the whole same constituency. Conservative policy identity can attract primary voters while narrowing other donors. 8–27 puts him above Kemp through greater national campaign exposure, but well below a majority even in systemic damage because coordination is unproven. This advantage is assumption-sensitive, not polling-derived.

ted_cruz.reason: Provisional hold after common comparison. Rubio competes for hawkish donors; Paul offers a different trade/restraint case. Tariff skepticism can distinguish Cruz without transferring all business voters to him. 3–8 assumes no current coordination advantage over either heir or executive rivals. An independent donor/organizer consolidation would challenge this low ceiling; it is a vulnerable judgment rather than a demonstrated limit.

faction_links.mechanism: Donor-facing positioning distinguishes him from Vance; the same hawkish networks also court Rubio, so factional preference is not an exclusive candidate coalition.

john_mcentee.reason: Provisional hold after common comparison. A plausible core is younger, culturally conservative Trump-aligned voters seeking original-program continuity with different leadership. Restraint voters are an extension, not Paul/Massie’s automatic transferable pool. Trump’s choice could keep this audience with Vance. 1–3 is carried provisionally because even a plausible program-continuity breakthrough must overcome entry and conversion against seven rivals. This narrow ceiling is not well validated: a wider plausible range remains unresolved. Hold under incomplete intake, not a finding that upside cannot exceed 3.

faction_links.mechanism: Historical personnel recruitment offers an executive-control capability relevant to this faction’s goals; that is a policy-channel analogy, not evidence that its current leaders support his nomination.
His actual 2020 withdrawal directive work could contest an exclusive claim to demonstrated restraint; no current endorsement, alliance or bloc of primary votes follows.

rand_paul.reason: Provisional hold after common comparison. Competes with Massie for constitutional-limit voters; free-trade business appeal may extend the pool but fiscal remedies need voter acceptance. Neither receives all opponents of the war. 6–15 values an established policy alternative most in systemic damage, below executive contenders because breadth and coordination are unverified. A larger cross-faction coalition would falsify the ceiling.

faction_links.mechanism: Existing policy dissent and oversight channels support an analytical campaign argument; inclusion in the forecast does not establish an endorsement, new faction alignment or voter transfer.

brian_kemp.reason: Provisional hold after common comparison. Competes with DeSantis for executive reset. Home-state support for considering a bid is not national preference; national coalition conversion is the required bridge. 10–20 is supported relatively by an electoral foothold but its high floor is weakly tested. Treat it as a provisional organization-transfer assumption; non-entry or failed early-state conversion would reduce it.

thomas_massie.reason: Provisional hold after common comparison. Overlaps Paul while offering costly dissent and accountability. A donor supporting both in other races does not create two exclusive presidential coalitions. 1–5 gives accountability upside above recovery while discounting party route and coalition width. Broader verified Republican organization would challenge the ceiling; neither defeat nor a protest audience sets a permanent cap.

faction_links.mechanism: Existing policy dissent and oversight channels support an analytical campaign argument; inclusion in the forecast does not establish an endorsement, new faction alignment or voter transfer.

gaps: Full two-index, 15-headline independent recall not completed: CNN restricted and Axios dated index unavailable; supplemental Just Security sampling is not a substitute.
Current comparable primary polling, campaign pledges and early-state organization remain unverified across the roster. Missing coverage is not absent support.
McEntee 1–3 scenario ceiling, Kemp 10–20 range and DeSantis relative advantage remain particularly assumption-sensitive; this hold is not quantitative validation.
All-issue legal outcomes, financial/FARA/ethics filings and personnel status census incomplete. Prior daily unresolved items remain open.
Unlisted contenders may capture the reset; conditional normalization conceals that risk. No full-field residual estimated.

wargame.target: Conditional probability of winning the 2028 Republican nomination given that one of the eight authorized candidates wins; not full-field odds.
wargame.horizon: Dominant environment during candidate entry, coalition formation and the 2028 Republican nomination contest; next checkpoints through early 2027.
wargame.summary: Persistent costs and accountability pressure still compete with retained Republican organization. No automatic outsider transfer is established. Retain the five environments and provisional eight-person mixture after common comparison; exact ceilings and floors remain weakly identified.
wargame.debate_mode: Structured single-analyst opposition and adjudication; no independent reviewers.
wargame.partition_rule: Classify by the dominant nomination mechanism: recovery requires durable substantive relief; systemic requires broad senior responsibility; selective requires accepted bounded responsibility without full recovery; backlash requires loyalty mobilization despite no recovery; managed_costs is the residual. Mixed events are not counted twice; weights describe which mechanism eventually dominates, conditional on this roster.
wargame.field_risk: Eight authorized contenders are modeled. Unlisted contenders can still win; influence or an independent presidential run does not count as winning the Republican nomination. No full-field residual is estimated.
wargame.weighting_note: Provisional hold after causal reconsideration, not fresh calibration. Managed costs and systemic damage each retain 30%; recovery 15%, selective reset 15%, backlash 10%. Shared intake rechecks the electoral problem and announced personnel change but does not identify changed primary support or sufficiently comparable organization to justify numerical revision. No new measured support change is claimed.

election_verdict.finding: The leading explanation is rejection of costly policy outcomes and self-serving priorities, amplified by weak candidates; this is not merely an unlucky campaign or a mandate against every conservative policy.
election_verdict.countercase: A midterm electorate differs from the next presidential primary electorate. Opposition turnout and local candidate quality can magnify a national defeat.
election_verdict.resolution: Treat affordability, war costs and accountability as a joint liability. Vance’s war-only diagnosis preserves his domestic program but leaves an opening on tariffs and administration priorities. Do not assign causal percentages from a survey.

responsibility.finding: Trump is the principal owner. Vance and Rubio cannot shed public advocacy and senior-office responsibility through retrospective criticism; Hegseth is a plausible concentrated target but not a sufficient explanation for economy-wide discontent.
responsibility.countercase: Voters can distinguish the president who ordered a policy, its operational managers and an adviser who argued for limits. A successful exit can differentiate the latter.
responsibility.resolution: Assign blame by the specific act, public defense and documentary chain, not association alone. Expect attempted scapegoating; whether it sticks depends on records and whether living conditions improve.

appeal_and_durability.finding: Vance has the strongest demonstrated starting route among the eight approved contenders. DeSantis and Kemp compete for executive competence outside the federal decision chain; Paul and Massie offer distinct but overlapping constitutional-limit challenges. No coalition transfer is yet demonstrated.
appeal_and_durability.countercase: Early recognition and patron access can be mistaken for durable attraction. An apparent outsider can also carry Trump-era baggage, past campaign weaknesses or state controversies.
appeal_and_durability.resolution: Discount familiar names and access when estimating future wins. A credible break needs a program, organizing and costly choices, while a continuity candidate needs results rather than a revised explanation.

democratic_power.finding: Expect investigations, preservation disputes, hearings and pressure over spending and confirmations once the new Congress organizes. This should keep responsibility and financial conflicts in the news rather than permit a clean messaging reset.
democratic_power.countercase: A congressional majority is not control of the executive. Vetoes, Senate procedure, litigation, competing legislative priorities and public fatigue constrain what Democrats can deliver.
democratic_power.resolution: Forecast sustained scrutiny more readily than immediate policy reversal, removal or prosecution. Obstruction or partisan excess can create a Republican rallying point; failure to lower costs can also redistribute blame toward Congress.

oversight_findings.finding: Politically damaging records about process, internal warnings and financial conflicts are more plausible than a uniform exoneration. A proven criminal case against any named contender is not established and is not the base-case requirement for political harm.
oversight_findings.countercase: An inquiry can repeat already-known allegations, encounter privilege or missing records, or fail to connect a conflict to a decision. Strong partisan rhetoric can outrun admissible evidence.
oversight_findings.resolution: Model systemic damage, selective accountability and weak-findings backlash separately. Criminal illegality, a substantiated ethics violation, misleading conduct and political embarrassment are different outcomes; do not forecast a particular person’s guilt from incentives.

loyalty_dilemma.finding: Selective differentiation is the most likely initial strategy: credit Trump and MAGA goals, blame implementation or advisers, promise competent correction. Vance’s timing makes an opportunism attack available to both hawks and restraint rivals.
loyalty_dilemma.countercase: Trump publicly welcomed Vance’s postmortem and Don Jr. supported the message in the existing record. Vance can criticize policy with permission; voters need not punish adaptation they see as learning.
loyalty_dilemma.resolution: The squeeze is real but not automatically fatal. The critical test is a costly forced choice: testimony, a funding limit, a dismissal or contradiction in documents. A debate attack matters if a credible rival and an audience amplify it, not merely because the line is available.

scenarios.name: Results rehabilitate continuity
scenarios.definition: A durable improvement in war and household costs dominates the nomination environment; serious revelations do not prevent leadership rehabilitation.
scenarios.weight_reason: Lower weight than persistent costs because an exit alone does not reverse inflation or repair trust; retained because two years allow meaningful change.
scenarios.sequence: Negotiation or policy correction produces visible relief; Trump claims vindication; networks consolidate behind an heir.
scenarios.falsifier: A settlement without cost relief or continuing credible records of misconduct would defeat the rehabilitation premise.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: Vance can claim the exit and retain Trump’s permission. Paul and Massie provide more explicit dissent alternatives, while entry and organization still favor the incumbent heir.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: Rubio’s security rationale regains value, conditional on entry.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: The need for a federal alternative recedes. Kemp now contests the same executive-reset lane; it is not an exclusive coalition.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: A narrower ideological lane survives, without a broad opening.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A demand for a wholly new figure remains small.
candidate_reasoning.rand_paul: His liberty critique persists, but improved outcomes weaken a rupture pitch.
candidate_reasoning.brian_kemp: Executive competence survives as a lane, with less need for a federal reset.
candidate_reasoning.thomas_massie: A successful reset narrows the insurgent opening; party entry remains uncertain.

scenarios.name: Costs persist; leadership retains a coalition
scenarios.definition: Neither recovery, systemic accountability, a convincing selective reset nor an oversight backlash becomes dominant; dissatisfaction persists but Republican leadership retains organizing capacity.
scenarios.weight_reason: A residual mixed environment is plausible: entrenched networks survive, while prolonged costs prevent a clean return to the inherited baseline.
scenarios.sequence: Voters remain dissatisfied; candidates selectively criticize execution; no rival fully coordinates defectors.
scenarios.falsifier: Clear rehabilitation, party-wide documentary repudiation or a successful scapegoat reset would move weight to another branch.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: He can adapt, but recurring costs and credibility attacks reduce his cushion. Paul and Massie provide more explicit dissent alternatives, while entry and organization still favor the incumbent heir.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: A loyalist alternative persists, limited by policy responsibility and entry.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: Distance offers a meaningful but unproven coordination point. Kemp now contests the same executive-reset lane; it is not an exclusive coalition.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: Tariff skepticism helps at the margin; hawkish overlap limits growth.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A niche exists but organizing is missing.
candidate_reasoning.rand_paul: Persistent costs give free trade and restraint a stronger argument, discounted for coalition breadth.
candidate_reasoning.brian_kemp: An alternative executive can attract some reset demand without a complete leadership repudiation.
candidate_reasoning.thomas_massie: Policy dissent has room, but Paul competes and national organization remains unproven.

scenarios.name: Accountability discredits the federal leadership
scenarios.definition: Credible disclosures or durable policy failure attach responsibility to senior leadership; a subordinate-only explanation does not satisfy an important Republican constituency. Criminal convictions are not required.
scenarios.weight_reason: War, household costs, demand for checks and documented investigative preparation justify substantial weight; absence of post-election primary data prevents making this the sole or majority scenario.
scenarios.sequence: Records or continued failure expose contradictions; donors and organizers consider alternatives; a credible rival turns attacks into coordination and early-state gains.
scenarios.falsifier: If primary voters retain confidence, disclosures fail to connect to senior decisions, or no alternative organizes, this branch is overstated.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: He retains a floor of access, but joint ownership and contradictory defenses are costly. Paul and Massie provide more explicit dissent alternatives, while entry and organization still favor the incumbent heir.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: Direct foreign-policy ownership and deference leave limited escape.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: An experienced state executive is the strongest approved coordination point, conditional on rebuilding. Kemp now contests the same executive-reset lane; it is not an exclusive coalition.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: He offers a non-executive fallback, discounted for hawkish responsibility.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A leadership vacuum helps a niche challenger, heavily discounted for insider baggage and entry gates.
candidate_reasoning.rand_paul: Earlier dissent matters more, but he must widen a coalition that overlaps Massie’s.
candidate_reasoning.brian_kemp: A credible executive outside the decision chain competes with DeSantis for defectors and donors.
candidate_reasoning.thomas_massie: Corroborated accountability can help, while primary defeat and a possible outside-party route cap the GOP path.

scenarios.name: Blame concentrates; an heir survives a reset
scenarios.definition: Credible accountability is concentrated on specific officials and accepted as bounded; correction creates space for a successor without broad leadership rehabilitation.
scenarios.weight_reason: Personnel pressure makes scapegoating plausible, but replacing a minister cannot alone erase prices, tariffs or vice-presidential responsibility.
scenarios.sequence: Hearings or a dismissal concentrate blame; Trump authorizes correction; an heir claims limits and competence while rivals test whether separation is credible.
scenarios.falsifier: Documents implicating the heir, continued economic deterioration or failed separation would push toward systemic damage or managed costs.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: Vance can support accountability with Trump’s permission; he is not inherently trapped on every choice. Paul and Massie provide more explicit dissent alternatives, while entry and organization still favor the incumbent heir.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: Hegseth-focused blame does not automatically absolve State advice or Rubio’s defenses.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: A partial reset leaves room to argue Washington cannot police itself. Kemp now contests the same executive-reset lane; it is not an exclusive coalition.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: A fallback benefits if rival heirs remain compromised.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A small opening persists without demonstrated electoral scale.
candidate_reasoning.rand_paul: Some corrective demand survives, but Trump-authorized blame limits the scope for a rupture.
candidate_reasoning.brian_kemp: He can argue a partial reset is insufficient while competing for the same executive lane as DeSantis.
candidate_reasoning.thomas_massie: A bounded scandal can validate particular concerns without making him a viable national nominee.

scenarios.name: Weak findings and partisan conflict restore loyalty
scenarios.definition: Investigations fail to persuade enough Republican voters and conflict with Democrats becomes the dominant organizing frame, without a substantive recovery.
scenarios.weight_reason: Retained as a countercase, not equal-weight balance: the documented demand for oversight makes assuming immediate backlash too optimistic for incumbents.
scenarios.sequence: Evidence disappoints or Democrats overreach; Republicans rally against Congress; Trump’s endorsement regains coordinating force.
scenarios.falsifier: Credible corroborated findings accepted within Republican networks or effective Democratic delivery would weaken this branch.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: The best-positioned authorized heir benefits, conditional on Trump maintaining permission. Paul and Massie provide more explicit dissent alternatives, while entry and organization still favor the incumbent heir.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: A loyalist campaign has room, though deference remains an entry constraint.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: A rupture pitch loses demand; he must compete on conservative governing performance. Kemp now contests the same executive-reset lane; it is not an exclusive coalition.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: An ideological lane survives but coordination favors the heir.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: A media-oriented alternative may gain attention but not necessarily delegates.
candidate_reasoning.rand_paul: Partisan rallying reduces demand for an insurgent, without erasing his established platform.
candidate_reasoning.brian_kemp: He can compete on governing performance, but the heir regains a coordinating advantage.
candidate_reasoning.thomas_massie: An insurgent or outside-party project struggles to win a loyalty-driven GOP nomination.

jd_vance.best_case: He retains fundraising, name recognition and succession channels while delivering a negotiated exit. Trump grants room to correct the policy; primary voters prefer an experienced heir to restarting the party.
jd_vance.failure_case: Post-defeat criticism looks retrospective. Documents or a Hegseth confrontation force him to defend conduct he privately questioned, abandon a colleague, or evade. Rivals use that record to make both loyalty and restraint claims untrustworthy.
jd_vance.rebuttal: The opposing case overstates a no-win trap. Trump can authorize blame of subordinates; replacing Hegseth could help Vance. Without compelling records or a viable rival, voters may reward a practical pivot rather than consistency.
jd_vance.verdict: Provisional hold after common comparison. Trump-aligned voters overlap McEntee; policy-restraint voters overlap Paul and Massie. Recovery can coordinate these groups behind an heir, while persistent costs permit defections without automatically delivering them to one rival. 16–52 reflects a viable heir even under systemic damage and the strongest coordination route in recovery/backlash. The high floor is vulnerable to actual organizer defection or refusal to run; it is not a measured loyal bloc.

adversarial_cases.continuity_recovery: Trump can permit a negotiated exit and preserve activist/fundraising coordination. Primary voters may reward adaptation; congressional conflict can reinforce loyalty even when general-election voters disapprove. This explains organizational persistence better than a universal repudiation thesis.
adversarial_cases.repudiation_accountability: Costs, priorities and scrutiny create several liability channels, not a war-only verdict. Records can impair senior credibility before any conviction. A credible executive or restrainer can coordinate defectors, but must actually enter and organize.
adversarial_cases.coalition_transfer_skeptic: A dissatisfied electorate is not a transferable primary coalition. Governors compete with each other; Paul/Massie overlap; McEntee overlaps Trump-aligned voters. Donors can decline all eight or choose an excluded contender.
adversarial_cases.adjudication: Persistent dissatisfaction with surviving party machinery is the central near-term judgment; systemic accountability remains an equally weighted longer-run environment rather than a proven outcome. wargame.partition_rule: Classify by the dominant nomination mechanism: recovery requires durable substantive relief; systemic requires broad senior responsibility; selective requires accepted bounded responsibility without full recovery; backlash requires loyalty mobilization despite no recovery; managed_costs is the residual. wargame.field_risk: Eight authorized contenders are modeled. Unlisted contenders can still win; influence or an independent presidential run does not count as winning the Republican nomination. No full-field residual is estimated.
