election_verdict.finding: The leading explanation is rejection of costly policy outcomes and self-serving priorities, amplified by weak candidates; this is not merely an unlucky campaign or a mandate against every conservative policy.
election_verdict.countercase: A midterm electorate differs from the next presidential primary electorate. Opposition turnout and local candidate quality can magnify a national defeat.
election_verdict.resolution: Treat affordability, war costs and accountability as a joint liability. Vance’s war-only diagnosis preserves his domestic program but leaves an opening on tariffs and administration priorities. Do not assign causal percentages from a survey.

responsibility.finding: Trump is the principal owner. Vance and Rubio cannot shed public advocacy and senior-office responsibility through retrospective criticism; Hegseth is a plausible concentrated target but not a sufficient explanation for economy-wide discontent.
responsibility.countercase: Voters can distinguish the president who ordered a policy, its operational managers and an adviser who argued for limits. A successful exit can differentiate the latter.
responsibility.resolution: Assign responsibility to the specific act and term: current executive advice/defense is not the same as first-term service, later transition planning, Senate advocacy or state office. Rivals can attack associations, but whether voters accept that bridge is forecast explicitly, not presumed.

appeal_and_durability.finding: Vance has the strongest demonstrated starting route among the eight approved contenders. DeSantis and Kemp compete for executive competence outside the federal decision chain; Paul and Massie offer distinct but overlapping constitutional-limit challenges. No coalition transfer is yet demonstrated.
appeal_and_durability.countercase: Early recognition and patron access can be mistaken for durable attraction. An apparent outsider can also carry Trump-era baggage, past campaign weaknesses or state controversies.
appeal_and_durability.resolution: Future enthusiasm, money, media and organization can reinforce one another for established and emerging contenders. No current asset fixes a permanent ceiling. Select a modest but meaningful McEntee breakthrough, lower Kemp’s assumed national floor and retain Vance’s comparative lead; do not infer a measured youth base.

democratic_power.finding: Expect investigations, preservation disputes, hearings and pressure over spending and confirmations once the new Congress organizes. This should keep responsibility and financial conflicts in the news rather than permit a clean messaging reset.
democratic_power.countercase: A congressional majority is not control of the executive. Vetoes, Senate procedure, litigation, competing legislative priorities and public fatigue constrain what Democrats can deliver.
democratic_power.resolution: Forecast sustained scrutiny more readily than immediate policy reversal, removal or prosecution. Obstruction or partisan excess can create a Republican rallying point; failure to lower costs can also redistribute blame toward Congress.

oversight_findings.finding: Politically damaging records about process, internal warnings and financial conflicts are more plausible than a uniform exoneration. A proven criminal case against any named contender is not established and is not the base-case requirement for political harm.
oversight_findings.countercase: An inquiry can repeat already-known allegations, encounter privilege or missing records, or fail to connect a conflict to a decision. Strong partisan rhetoric can outrun admissible evidence.
oversight_findings.resolution: Model systemic damage, selective accountability and weak-findings backlash separately. Criminal illegality, a substantiated ethics violation, misleading conduct and political embarrassment are different outcomes; do not forecast a particular person’s guilt from incentives.

loyalty_dilemma.finding: Selective differentiation is the most likely initial strategy: credit Trump and MAGA goals, blame implementation or advisers, promise competent correction. Vance’s timing makes an opportunism attack available to both hawks and restraint rivals.
loyalty_dilemma.countercase: Trump publicly welcomed Vance’s postmortem and Don Jr. supported the message in the existing record. Vance can criticize policy with permission; voters need not punish adaptation they see as learning.
loyalty_dilemma.resolution: The squeeze is real but not automatically fatal. The critical test is a costly forced choice: testimony, a funding limit, a dismissal or contradiction in documents. A debate attack matters if a credible rival and an audience amplify it, not merely because the line is available.

faction_links.mechanism: Existing policy dissent and oversight channels support an analytical campaign argument; inclusion in the forecast does not establish an endorsement, new faction alignment or voter transfer.

gaps: Conditional forecast covers only the eight authorized candidates; unlisted contenders can win.
No comprehensive current filings, media-stream or early-state organizer census; groups are mostly potential presidential constituencies.
Personal appeal is largely qualitative and historically grounded; the 2024 debate-watcher poll is not current Republican preference.
Full recall, personnel, lobbying and 2–8-week high-impact falsifier audit remain incomplete.

wargame.target: Conditional probability of winning the 2028 Republican nomination given that one of the eight authorized candidates wins; not full-field odds.
wargame.horizon: Dominant environment during candidate entry, coalition formation and the 2028 Republican nomination contest; next checkpoints through early 2027.
wargame.summary: Vance remains the leading contender because established relationships can sustain a campaign while rivals compete for overlapping supporters. His ability to present policy correction as credible leadership is central. Governors can benefit from rejection of federal leadership; liberty candidates and McEntee must also turn a distinct argument and personal appeal into willing organizers and voters. None receives disaffected supporters automatically.
wargame.debate_mode: Structured single-analyst opposition; no separate reviewer participated.
wargame.partition_rule: Classify by the dominant nomination mechanism: recovery requires durable substantive relief; systemic requires broad senior responsibility; selective requires accepted bounded responsibility without full recovery; backlash requires loyalty mobilization despite no recovery; managed_costs is the residual. Mixed events are not counted twice; weights describe which mechanism eventually dominates, conditional on this roster.
wargame.field_risk: Eight authorized contenders are modeled. Unlisted contenders can still win; influence or an independent presidential run does not count as winning the Republican nomination. No full-field residual is estimated.
wargame.weighting_note: Weekly affirmative hold after causal, appeal and support-base adjudication. Retain weights 15/30/30/15/10: the strongest alternatives remain persistent dissatisfaction with leadership organization and broad responsibility for federal failure. Trump’s conditional talk preference does not yet justify transferring ten points from systemic to recovery. Each candidate’s concrete alternative shares and mixture effects remain in comparison_review; the new appeal/base analysis favors the selected paths over those alternatives. No new formula, candidate, independent multiplier or missing-coverage penalty was used. Local arithmetic reproduces the prescribed mixture; sibling restrictions prevent direct use of the separate wargame script.

election_verdict.finding: The leading explanation is rejection of costly policy outcomes and self-serving priorities, amplified by weak candidates; this is not merely an unlucky campaign or a mandate against every conservative policy.
election_verdict.countercase: A midterm electorate differs from the next presidential primary electorate. Opposition turnout and local candidate quality can magnify a national defeat.
election_verdict.resolution: Treat affordability, war costs and accountability as a joint liability. Vance’s war-only diagnosis preserves his domestic program but leaves an opening on tariffs and administration priorities. Do not assign causal percentages from a survey.

responsibility.finding: Trump is the principal owner. Vance and Rubio cannot shed public advocacy and senior-office responsibility through retrospective criticism; Hegseth is a plausible concentrated target but not a sufficient explanation for economy-wide discontent.
responsibility.countercase: Voters can distinguish the president who ordered a policy, its operational managers and an adviser who argued for limits. A successful exit can differentiate the latter.
responsibility.resolution: Assign responsibility to the specific act and term: current executive advice/defense is not the same as first-term service, later transition planning, Senate advocacy or state office. Rivals can attack associations, but whether voters accept that bridge is forecast explicitly, not presumed.

appeal_and_durability.finding: Vance has the strongest demonstrated starting route among the eight approved contenders. DeSantis and Kemp compete for executive competence outside the federal decision chain; Paul and Massie offer distinct but overlapping constitutional-limit challenges. No coalition transfer is yet demonstrated.
appeal_and_durability.countercase: Early recognition and patron access can be mistaken for durable attraction. An apparent outsider can also carry Trump-era baggage, past campaign weaknesses or state controversies.
appeal_and_durability.resolution: Future enthusiasm, money, media and organization can reinforce one another for established and emerging contenders. No current asset fixes a permanent ceiling. Select a modest but meaningful McEntee breakthrough, lower Kemp’s assumed national floor and retain Vance’s comparative lead; do not infer a measured youth base.

democratic_power.finding: Expect investigations, preservation disputes, hearings and pressure over spending and confirmations once the new Congress organizes. This should keep responsibility and financial conflicts in the news rather than permit a clean messaging reset.
democratic_power.countercase: A congressional majority is not control of the executive. Vetoes, Senate procedure, litigation, competing legislative priorities and public fatigue constrain what Democrats can deliver.
democratic_power.resolution: Forecast sustained scrutiny more readily than immediate policy reversal, removal or prosecution. Obstruction or partisan excess can create a Republican rallying point; failure to lower costs can also redistribute blame toward Congress.

oversight_findings.finding: Politically damaging records about process, internal warnings and financial conflicts are more plausible than a uniform exoneration. A proven criminal case against any named contender is not established and is not the base-case requirement for political harm.
oversight_findings.countercase: An inquiry can repeat already-known allegations, encounter privilege or missing records, or fail to connect a conflict to a decision. Strong partisan rhetoric can outrun admissible evidence.
oversight_findings.resolution: Model systemic damage, selective accountability and weak-findings backlash separately. Criminal illegality, a substantiated ethics violation, misleading conduct and political embarrassment are different outcomes; do not forecast a particular person’s guilt from incentives.

loyalty_dilemma.finding: Selective differentiation is the most likely initial strategy: credit Trump and MAGA goals, blame implementation or advisers, promise competent correction. Vance’s timing makes an opportunism attack available to both hawks and restraint rivals.
loyalty_dilemma.countercase: Trump publicly welcomed Vance’s postmortem and Don Jr. supported the message in the existing record. Vance can criticize policy with permission; voters need not punish adaptation they see as learning.
loyalty_dilemma.resolution: The squeeze is real but not automatically fatal. The critical test is a costly forced choice: testimony, a funding limit, a dismissal or contradiction in documents. A debate attack matters if a credible rival and an audience amplify it, not merely because the line is available.

scenarios.name: Peace and lower household costs restore Republican confidence in Trump’s allies
scenarios.definition: War conditions and household costs improve enough that Republican voters regain confidence in Trump’s allies. Later disclosures do not undo that recovery.
scenarios.weight_reason: 15%: meaningful recovery has two years to occur, but settlement alone need not repair household costs or credibility. A 25% recovery alternative overstates relief without an implemented exit and durable improvement.
scenarios.sequence: If peace and household relief restore confidence, voters have less reason to gamble on an unfamiliar alternative. Candidates then compete for voters, donors and willing campaign staff; an endorsement or policy disagreement alone does not decide that competition.
scenarios.falsifier: A settlement without cost relief or continuing credible records of misconduct would defeat the rehabilitation premise.

candidate_reasoning.jd_vance: Vance would claim credit for negotiations and offer corrections while trying to retain Trump’s support. Loyalists may accept correction from an ally; voters who blame senior officials may distrust the same argument. He can recruit early-state staff through existing political relationships; disappointed activists can still defect.
candidate_reasoning.marco_rubio: Rubio would defend his foreign-policy judgment and decide whether to seek an independent mandate rather than support Vance. Security-minded voters can value experience; war-weary voters may see him as responsible for the policy they reject. Former campaign and official contacts could recruit staff; current office does not supply a presidential delegate team.
candidate_reasoning.ron_desantis: DeSantis would contrast Florida governance with federal failures and try to rebuild a more disciplined presidential team. Policy-focused conservatives may welcome a forceful governor; others may prefer Kemp’s manner or remain loyal to Trump’s allies. A rebuilt national team could combine former staff with defectors; the 2024 campaign is experience rather than a ready-made operation.
candidate_reasoning.ted_cruz: Cruz would combine conservative credentials with criticism of economic decisions and seek an opening against Vance and Rubio. Religious activists may reward conviction; less ideological voters may want a governor or a less combative candidate. He could reactivate old organizers and recruit new ones, provided they choose this race over rival campaigns.
candidate_reasoning.john_mcentee: McEntee could distinguish first-term personnel and withdrawal work from present federal decisions, while defending his later Project 2025 role. Some Trump-aligned voters may welcome a fresh messenger; others may prefer an elected official or question his readiness and record. Recruitment experience could help hire election specialists if willing supporters emerge; transition staffing is not delegate organizing.
candidate_reasoning.rand_paul: Paul would make a case for limits on war and spending while trying to keep voters who still support much of Trump’s agenda. Principle-focused Republicans may trust costly disagreement; other loyalists may prefer a candidate endorsed by Trump. Political contacts can recruit organizers beyond Kentucky if interest broadens; cooperation with Massie does not guarantee a presidential endorsement.
candidate_reasoning.brian_kemp: Kemp would emphasize governing results and independence from federal decisions while deciding whether to pursue a national race. Voters seeking a governor may find him reassuring; social-policy disagreements and loyalty objections can narrow that appeal. Georgia allies could recruit early-state specialists if he enters and attracts national demand.
candidate_reasoning.thomas_massie: Massie would press accountability and war-powers claims and must choose whether a presidential effort would stay inside the Republican Party. Antiwar and accountability voters may value conviction; party loyalists may see obstruction rather than leadership. Activists could recruit state specialists if he chooses a Republican campaign; oversight publicity alone will not qualify delegates.

jd_vance.best_case: He retains fundraising, name recognition and succession channels while delivering a negotiated exit. Trump grants room to correct the policy; primary voters prefer an experienced heir to restarting the party.
jd_vance.failure_case: Post-defeat criticism looks retrospective. Documents or a Hegseth confrontation force him to defend conduct he privately questioned, abandon a colleague, or evade. Rivals use that record to make both loyalty and restraint claims untrustworthy.
jd_vance.rebuttal: Loyalists may accept correction from an ally; voters who blame senior officials may distrust the same argument. Existing fundraisers can keep introductions and activist recruitment moving, but may resist policies that harm their own priorities. Policy agreement is not enough to establish a presidential choice.
jd_vance.verdict: He can explain conservative policies in a more measured setting and offer continuity with a change of course. Changing his defense of the war can look like shifting blame rather than independent judgment. He can recruit early-state staff through existing political relationships; disappointed activists can still defect.
jd_vance.entry_assessment: Entry is plausible but undeclared in this intake. If running, existing succession channels give a stronger starting route than the other seven; neither office nor recognition guarantees nomination. Current pledges and early-state presidential roles remain incompletely verified; no absent-coverage penalty.
jd_vance.next_move: Distinguish advice from orders and choose which current decisions to defend. Test actual entry and state recruitment before interpreting publicity as a campaign.
jd_vance.rival_attack: A rival can contrast private objections, public defenses and the timing after defeat: why trust another pivot? A hawk can attack abandonment; a restrainer can demand proof of a costly pre-election objection.
jd_vance.durability_test: Actual peace and lower costs would blunt a consistency attack. Repeated incompatible defenses, documentary contradiction or loss of Trump-backed organizers would make the squeeze consequential rather than rhetorical.
jd_vance.resource_and_response_review: Carried RNC, Rockbridge and Turning Point channels offer mobilizable fundraisers and activists. Treat access as capacity, not exclusively controlled campaign assets; verify current commitments as for every rival. Expected Trump/rival reaction is conditional: grant permission, contest loyalty or recruit overlapping organizers; no actual endorsement or donor choice is inferred.

marco_rubio.best_case: An experienced security official can inherit loyalists who distrust Vance’s pivot, draw on hawkish donor access and argue the problem was execution rather than the original objectives.
marco_rubio.failure_case: If the policy itself is repudiated, credentials become ownership. Hearings put his explanations alongside internal warnings, while deference to Vance or failure to enter prevents conversion of donor preference into a campaign.
marco_rubio.rebuttal: Security-minded voters can value experience; war-weary voters may see him as responsible for the policy they reject. Interested donors could finance recruitment if he enters, but a preference is not a pledge and Cruz seeks overlapping backers. Policy agreement is not enough to establish a presidential choice.
marco_rubio.verdict: His family narrative and conversational humor can make a national-security argument approachable. Serving Trump while deferring on a bid can make him seem unwilling to lead independently. Former campaign and official contacts could recruit staff; current office does not supply a presidential delegate team.
marco_rubio.entry_assessment: An independent entry is less assured than his visibility suggests because of carried deference to Vance. Conditional on entering, national experience and donor access make him competitive. Current pledges and early-state presidential roles remain incompletely verified; no absent-coverage penalty.
marco_rubio.next_move: Separate specific advice from outcomes without erasing public advocacy. Test actual entry and state recruitment before interpreting publicity as a campaign.
marco_rubio.rival_attack: An outsider can ask why the foreign-policy expert did not anticipate the costs. Vance can claim to have offered the exit while Rubio defended the initial course.
marco_rubio.durability_test: Watch an independent fundraising/endorsement operation, entry statements and testimony tying advice to decisions. A defensible settlement strengthens his case; proof public claims diverged from internal assessments weakens it.
marco_rubio.resource_and_response_review: Policy relationships and prospective financiers can be mobilized; donor preference is not a campaign pledge. Apply the same allowance to future staff recruitment as to governors and newcomers. Expected Trump/rival reaction is conditional: grant permission, contest loyalty or recruit overlapping organizers; no actual endorsement or donor choice is inferred.

ron_desantis.best_case: He offers governing experience without current federal command responsibility. Donors and primary voters seeking a new direction can coordinate around him if Washington’s leaders remain discredited.
ron_desantis.failure_case: Distance is mistaken for popularity. His earlier intervention statements, state accountability exposure and past campaign problems prevent a clean break, while donors prefer someone outside the approved roster.
ron_desantis.rebuttal: Policy-focused conservatives may welcome a forceful governor; others may prefer Kemp’s manner or remain loyal to Trump’s allies. Past donors can return if he offers a credible plan, but prior execution and policy disputes can push them to another governor. Policy agreement is not enough to establish a presidential choice.
ron_desantis.verdict: He can present a record of carrying out conservative policies as evidence that he would act decisively. His previous campaign exposed problems connecting policy accomplishments to personal enthusiasm. A rebuilt national team could combine former staff with defectors; the 2024 campaign is experience rather than a ready-made operation.
ron_desantis.entry_assessment: No presidential entry confirmed; the current entry account is contested. Conditional competitiveness rests on executive experience and a past national effort, not presumed ownership of all dissatisfaction. Current commitments remain incompletely verified.
ron_desantis.next_move: Lead a conservative reset while distinguishing state acts from current federal decisions. Test actual entry and state recruitment before interpreting publicity as a campaign.
ron_desantis.rival_attack: Vance can cite prior support for force and the failed earlier campaign. Rivals can test whether state controversies undermine an accountability pitch.
ron_desantis.durability_test: Require current donors, organizers, early-state activity and voter response to the contrast; absence of those developments should erode the inferred opening.
ron_desantis.resource_and_response_review: Past campaign relationships and fundraising experience can be rebuilt. The 2023 record documents execution and donor problems; it neither proves present donor desertion nor guarantees a new national operation. Expected Trump/rival reaction is conditional: grant permission, contest loyalty or recruit overlapping organizers; no actual endorsement or donor choice is inferred.

ted_cruz.best_case: He has a recognizable conservative identity and a tariff-skeptical argument on costs. As a non-executive contender he can exploit division between administration heirs and seek religious-conservative organization.
ted_cruz.failure_case: A hawkish record limits separation from intervention, Rubio competes for donors and recognition does not produce coalition growth. Past repositioning and judgment controversies remain usable.
ted_cruz.rebuttal: Religious activists may reward conviction; less ideological voters may want a governor or a less combative candidate. Past backers can help him re-enter, but security and business donors have Rubio and other alternatives. Policy agreement is not enough to establish a presidential choice.
ted_cruz.verdict: His detailed, combative arguments can signal conviction and preparation to conservative activists. Voters tired of partisan combat may see the same style as rigid, while shifts toward Trump invite trust attacks. He could reactivate old organizers and recruit new ones, provided they choose this race over rival campaigns.
ted_cruz.entry_assessment: Entry is uncertain; conditional on running he has a recognizable conservative identity and prior presidential experience. Familiarity is not evidence of coalition growth. Current pledges and early-state presidential roles remain incompletely verified; no absent-coverage penalty.
ted_cruz.next_move: Distinguish legislative choices from executive orders and propose a conservative correction. Test actual entry and state recruitment before interpreting publicity as a campaign.
ted_cruz.rival_attack: Rivals can ask how a hawkish alternative escapes the same war verdict, and why this campaign would consolidate support his previous effort did not.
ted_cruz.durability_test: A distinct cost-of-living coalition and current organizational commitments matter more than recycled 2016 donor names.
ted_cruz.resource_and_response_review: Senate and historical religious-conservative/donor relationships are potentially mobilizable. No new campaign pledges are verified; do not favor historical access over newcomers’ transferable relationships automatically. Expected Trump/rival reaction is conditional: grant permission, contest loyalty or recruit overlapping organizers; no actual endorsement or donor choice is inferred.

john_mcentee.best_case: Personnel and withdrawal experience can support a substantive nationalist challenge when established contenders fail; a smaller media-driven opening can become electorally useful if organization follows.
john_mcentee.failure_case: He is himself a Trump-era insider. Prior conduct, electoral-count work and business scrutiny complicate a clean-accountability pitch, and historical business financing does not supply a campaign.
john_mcentee.rebuttal: Some Trump-aligned voters may welcome a fresh messenger; others may prefer an elected official or question his readiness and record. Commercial contacts could open introductions, but neither investment nor lobbying income is committed presidential funding. Policy agreement is not enough to establish a presidential choice.
john_mcentee.verdict: Informal political communication could make an unfamiliar candidate approachable to some conservative viewers. Attention to short-form content does not show that viewers trust him to govern or will work for a campaign. cross_candidate_challenges.issue: Rebuilding and liabilities mapped to actual audiences

cross_candidate_challenges.issue: Entry, resource access and present-policy responsibility

cross_candidate_challenges.issue: Restraint coalition, entry route and acquired organization

wargame.target: Conditional probability of winning the 2028 Republican nomination given that one of the eight authorized candidates wins; not full-field odds.
wargame.horizon: Dominant environment during candidate entry, coalition formation and the 2028 Republican nomination contest; next checkpoints through early 2027.
wargame.summary: Vance remains the leading contender, but recruiting supporters requires a willing candidate and a Republican campaign. DeSantis can pursue voters seeking a governor; Paul can seek antiwar Republicans who do not follow a third-party effort.
wargame.debate_mode: Structured single-analyst opposition; no independent reviewer.
wargame.partition_rule: Classify by the dominant nomination mechanism: recovery requires durable substantive relief; systemic requires broad senior responsibility; selective requires accepted bounded responsibility without full recovery; backlash requires loyalty mobilization despite no recovery; managed_costs is the residual. Mixed events are not counted twice; weights describe which mechanism eventually dominates, conditional on this roster.
wargame.field_risk: Eight authorized contenders are modeled. Unlisted contenders can still win; influence or an independent presidential run does not count as winning the Republican nomination. No full-field residual is estimated.
wargame.weighting_note: Weights remain 15/30/30/15/10 after competing recovery, accountability and transfer-skeptic cases. Within-branch correction moves Rubio→DeSantis one point in four environments and Massie→Paul zero to two points. These are causal judgments, not measured transfer rates. No missing-audit hold rule; candidate alternatives and weight stresses are recorded separately.

election_verdict.finding: The leading explanation is rejection of costly policy outcomes and self-serving priorities, amplified by weak candidates; this is not merely an unlucky campaign or a mandate against every conservative policy.
election_verdict.countercase: A midterm electorate differs from the next presidential primary electorate. Opposition turnout and local candidate quality can magnify a national defeat.
election_verdict.resolution: Treat affordability, war costs and accountability as a joint liability. Vance’s war-only diagnosis preserves his domestic program but leaves an opening on tariffs and administration priorities. Do not assign causal percentages from a survey.

responsibility.finding: Trump is the principal owner. Vance and Rubio cannot shed public advocacy and senior-office responsibility through retrospective criticism; Hegseth is a plausible concentrated target but not a sufficient explanation for economy-wide discontent.
responsibility.countercase: Voters can distinguish the president who ordered a policy, its operational managers and an adviser who argued for limits. A successful exit can differentiate the latter.
responsibility.resolution: Assign responsibility to the specific act and term: current executive advice/defense is not the same as first-term service, later transition planning, Senate advocacy or state office. Rivals can attack associations, but whether voters accept that bridge is forecast explicitly, not presumed.

appeal_and_durability.finding: Vance has the strongest demonstrated starting route among the eight approved contenders. DeSantis and Kemp compete for executive competence outside the federal decision chain; Paul and Massie offer distinct but overlapping constitutional-limit challenges. No coalition transfer is yet demonstrated.
appeal_and_durability.countercase: Early recognition and patron access can be mistaken for durable attraction. An apparent outsider can also carry Trump-era baggage, past campaign weaknesses or state controversies.
appeal_and_durability.resolution: Future enthusiasm, money, media and organization can reinforce one another for established and emerging contenders. No current asset fixes a permanent ceiling. Select a modest but meaningful McEntee breakthrough, lower Kemp’s assumed national floor and retain Vance’s comparative lead; do not infer a measured youth base.

democratic_power.finding: Expect investigations, preservation disputes, hearings and pressure over spending and confirmations once the new Congress organizes. This should keep responsibility and financial conflicts in the news rather than permit a clean messaging reset.
democratic_power.countercase: A congressional majority is not control of the executive. Vetoes, Senate procedure, litigation, competing legislative priorities and public fatigue constrain what Democrats can deliver.
democratic_power.resolution: Credible countercase: centrist demands for affordability can constrain an expansive impeachment agenda. Retain oversight and partisan-backlash paths as distinct possibilities; congressional control is not executive control.

oversight_findings.finding: Politically damaging records about process, internal warnings and financial conflicts are more plausible than a uniform exoneration. A proven criminal case against any named contender is not established and is not the base-case requirement for political harm.
oversight_findings.countercase: An inquiry can repeat already-known allegations, encounter privilege or missing records, or fail to connect a conflict to a decision. Strong partisan rhetoric can outrun admissible evidence.
oversight_findings.resolution: Model systemic damage, selective accountability and weak-findings backlash separately. Criminal illegality, a substantiated ethics violation, misleading conduct and political embarrassment are different outcomes; do not forecast a particular person’s guilt from incentives.

loyalty_dilemma.finding: Trump permits Vance to speak while reminding audiences that Vance participated in decisions. That creates room for correction and a present credibility vulnerability at the same time.
loyalty_dilemma.countercase: Voters can see adaptation as learning rather than blame-shifting, especially if negotiations produce results.
loyalty_dilemma.resolution: Credible countercase: do not infer mass rejection or immunity. Preserve Vance’s lead while testing trust through support and organizing choices.

findings.finding: Broad ordering is consistent: Vance has the clearest organization, Rubio a credible alternative, Cruz a narrower competing lane. DeSantis and McEntee require more coalition-building assumptions.

Faction evidence does not calibrate precise probabilities. The 1.30-point Rubio–DeSantis gap and McEntee’s 3.90 are particularly assumption-sensitive. No exact reallocation is justified by this consistency pass alone.

Corrected the omission of historical immigration-oriented staffing and strengthened executive-control experience. Confirmed withdrawal drafting/signature involvement in the primary committee record. Do not reduce him to a content creator.
Use current faction homes; populist is a dissolved archival faction. Do not invent a unified media/insurgent constituency or automatically assign it to any nominee.
Miller/Wiles transition and Trump endorsement uncertainty affect the channels all contenders must navigate; none is an automatic nomination preference.
No conversion of legacy faction scores to odds; observed support, ideological preference, business investment, paid clients and prospective coalition transfer remain separate.

faction_consistency_review.probability_decision: All five percentages held as provisional starting judgments; consistency is not statistical calibration.
